To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduction of cytochromes by amicyanins occurs at different rates and extents depending on the presence or absence of the MADH cofactor tryptophan-tryptophylquinol (TTQ).

the electron transfer between cytochrome c551i and amicyanin occurs at different rates when amicyanins are free and when they are complexed with methylamine dehydrogenases, and that the rate of the reaction is dependent on the concentration of the methylamine dehydrogense.

the reduction of cytochromes by the blue copper proteins of the amicyanin family occurs much more slowly when the copper protein is free in solution than when it is in a complex with methylamine dehydrogenases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of proteins and protein complexes.
the study of the interactions between soluble redox proteins in the respiratory chain of Paracoccus denitrificans.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of electron transfer between proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amicyanins are not simple electron carriers, but that the electron transfer pathway from MADH to cytochrome depends on the presence of the complex.
the electron-transfer pathway from amicyanin through cytochrome c551i is not the same as that through cytochrome cd1, but the details are not yet known.

the electron transfer from amicyanin bound to MADH to cytochrome is more rapid than that from free amicyanin because the former reaction is facilitated by the binding of amicyaninand cytochrome to the MADH complex, and the latter is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron transfer pathway is altered by the complex formation between amicyanin and cytochrome.
the complex of amicyanins and MADH is required for electron transfer to cytochrome.
the electron transfer pathway is changed by the formation of the complex between MADH and amicyanin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron transfer pathway from the tryptopan-tryptophylquinol cofactor in MADH to cytochrome is altered when amicyanins is in a complex with MADH.
amicyanins bind to the surface of the cytochrome c, but the binding site is different for amicyanin alone and amicyanin bound to methylamine dehydrogenases.
amicyanins and cytochromes c-551 are able to form a complex in the absence of methylamine dehydrogenases.
